answer:
The 2013 Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering was awarded to five pioneers for their foundational work on the Internet and the World‑Wide Web:

| Recipient | Country | Affiliation at the time of the award |
|-----------|---------|--------------------------------------|
| Robert Kahn | United States | AT&T |
| Vinton Cerf | United States | AT&T |
| Louis Pouzin | France | INRIA |
| Sir Tim Berners‑Lee | United Kingdom | University of Cambridge |
| Marc Andreessen | United States | Netscape |

None of these five recipients were faculty, researchers, or students affiliated with the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT) when the award was given. Therefore, there was no “scientist at MIT” who received the Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering in 2013, and consequently there is no “father of the scientist at MIT” to identify in this context.
